title: Safety and efficacy of apixaban versus warfarin in peritoneal dialysis patients with non valvular atrial fibrillation: a randomized controlled trial
official: Safety and efficacy of apixaban versus warfarin in peritoneal dialysis patients with non valvular atrial fibrillation: a randomized controlled trial
summary: Main objective: To compare the safety of apixaban versus warfarin, comparing the incidence of the endpoint Bleeding
conditions: patients with end-stage renal disease on chronic peritoneal dialysis and with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men and women, aged at least 18 years, with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) treated with peritoneal dialysis for ≥ 3 months.
2. Patients with a history of non-valvular atrial fibrillation treated with oral anticoagulation or patients starting oral anticoagulation for a diagnosis of non-valvular atrial fibrillation
3. CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥ 2.
4. For women of childbearing age and sexually active, use of an effective method of contraception
5. Signing of informed consent
6. Affiliation to a social security scheme
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients not considered candidates for oral anticoagulation (active bleeding, recent gastrointestinal bleeding, severe hepatic impairment)
2. History of anaphylactic reaction to apixaban
3. Use of millepertuis (potent CYP3A4 inducer).
4. - Use of powerful inhibitors of CYP3A4 and gp-P: o azole antifungals (ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, miconazole - systemic route and oral gel) o HIV protease inhibitors.
5. Taking acetylsalicylic acid in doses of 500 mg per dose to 3 g per day
6. Patient with history of TIA or stroke in the 3 months preceding inclusion
7. Patient treated with hemodialysis (hybrid dialysis)
8. Moderate or severe mitral stenosis
9. Conditions other than non-valvular atrial fibrillation requiring anticoagulation, such as mechanical prosthetic valves, anti-phospholipid syndrome
10. Life expectancy less than 3 months
11. Registration on the waiting list for a kidney transplant with a cadaveric donor
12. Pregnant or breastfeeding woman
13. Patient under legal protection (Curatelle-Tutelle – Protection of justice)
